title: Multi-homed ejection profiles and load-fracturing policy for cross-region SLO resilience
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem: During cross-region incidents we observe sharp cascades where one region's overload causes downstream hedging/evacuation into partner regions, producing simultaneous SLA degradation across multiple homes. Existing policies use blunt geo-preference and uniform shedding which either overloads healthy regions or causes expensive ejections and cold fallbacks.

Goal: Design and implement a multi-homed ejection and "load-fracturing" steering policy that: (1) respects per-region latency SLOs, (2) enables fractional, proportional shedding across eligible regions to avoid single-region flood, (3) integrates with circuit-breaker states and autoscaler signals, and (4) supports safe rollout via canary knobs and conservative defaults.

Key concepts introduced: 
- Ejection profile: a weighted set of candidate regions with time-decayed penalties and hysteresis.
- Load fracturing: instead of 100% failing over, split a percentage of incoming traffic across N healthy regions proportionally to their available capacity and latency headroom.
- Soft circuit breaker: per-region score combining SLO burn rate, queue depth, KV cache miss rate; triggers graded throttling tiers rather than binary open/closed.

Design decisions and trade-offs: 
- Latency-first routing: baseline routing prioritizes regions meeting 95th percentile latency SLO. Candidate selection will filter out regions beyond the latency floor + configurable slack. This reduces user-visible tail latency at the cost of capacity utilization.
- Proportional shedding vs strict pinning: we favor proportional shedding to reduce cascade risk; however, customers who require strict locality can opt into a "pin-preservation" mode (enterprise-only).
- Metric signals: use combined signals (P95 latency, request queue length, CPU-backed GPU saturation metric, and model-kv-cache hit ratio) to compute region health score. Single signal triggers are avoided to reduce oscillation.
- Safety: include global circuit-breaker that enforces a max ejection rate and an emergency global fallback to pre-configured lightweight CPU-backed model variants when all GPU regions are degraded.

Implementation plan: 
1) Health scoring service (stateless): aggregates sliding-window metrics per region and exports a normalized health score (0..100). (Backend infra + small aggregator microservice)
2) Steering policy engine: implements ejection profiles, proportional fracturing algorithms (waterfilling allocator), and soft CB tiers. Expose config via console: ejection_window, hysteresis_ms, fracture_step_pct, min_fallback_capacity.
3) Router integration: the global request director will query steering engine and apply per-request route decisions (with fast path cache for small windows). Add token-aware consistent hashing adjustments to preserve locality while allowing fractioned routing.
4) Safety nets and rollouts: default conservative thresholds, with experiment flags for Canary and Gradual ramp (10% -> 50% -> 100%).

Acceptance criteria: 
- Unit and integration tests for allocator determinism and stability under synthetic oscillations.
- Synthetic soak test: simulate region A overload and verify that load fracturing keeps target P95 under SLO for at least 90% of samples and that no single region receives >1.6x of its steady baseline load.
- Dashboard: per-region health score, fracture allocation percent, and per-route latency/cost breakouts visible in Console.
- Rollout: feature gated in runtime-2.4 canary for 3 customers, monitors for 72h without regressions, then broader enabling.

Risks and mitigation: 
- Oscillation: use time-decayed penalties and minimum reallocation windows to dampen flapping.
- Metric noise: require at least two independent signals crossing thresholds to escalate CB state.
- Customer locality requirements: provide opt-out configuration and evaluate privacy/SLA implications for Private deployments.

Links and artifacts: 
- Design doc (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RES/Multi-Homed+Ejection+Profiles
- Simulation harness repo: https://github.com/redwood/resilience-sim/tree/eng-208771
- Draft console mockups (Drive): https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/1FractureConsoleMock

Next steps: finalize health score equation, implement steering engine prototype, and schedule a cross-team sync with Console and Product for config UX.
